submission.name: AidCall Drill
submission.tagline: Practice the first few minutes of a campus emergency response through voice-led scenarios.
submission.inspiration: On a large campus, a student or staff member may have to report an incident before they know which details responders need. We wanted to turn emergency guidance into a short decision game, and borrowed the idea of a voice front desk that gathers context and routes urgent information for review.
submission.what_it_does: The player works through a simulated campus incident, choosing actions as new details arrive and answering a Gemini dispatcher that asks follow-up questions. At the end, the app creates a brief report and reads key points aloud; the experience works from start to finish, though dispatcher responses sometimes repeat or lag.
submission.how_we_built_it: We built the scenario interface in React with Tailwind, and used Gemini to generate context-aware dispatcher prompts and a closing review from the player's choices. Browser speech input captures replies and Google Cloud Text-to-Speech voices the dispatcher, while a simple campus map model uses locations and connections to shape available actions.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: Keeping the voice exchange aligned with the game state was unreliable, and the dispatcher can repeat a prompt or miss part of an answer. Our campus locations are a small modeled set, so the route choices are not a live map or a substitute for official emergency procedures.
submission.accomplishments: We connected scenario choices, a contextual dispatcher, and a spoken wrap-up into a playable emergency practice loop. We are proud that Gemini can use the player's current situation to make the conversation feel tied to the exercise.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned to give a language model constrained context when its answer needs to match a game state, and saw how much timing matters in a voice interface. The voice-front-desk pattern also helped us think about collecting useful details before routing an incident for human review.
submission.whats_next: We would make turn-taking more reliable, add more campus scenarios, and review the guidance with university emergency staff. A future version could let teams coordinate roles during a drill and produce a clearer handoff report.
